t:
(a) Designation.—The Federal Bureau of Investigation building under construction at the intersection of 120th and L Streets in Omaha, Nebraska, shall be known and designated as the “J. James Exon Federal Bureau of Investigation Building”. 
    (b) References.—Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the building referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the J. James Exon Federal Bureau of Investigation Building.

fable.w: This section only names a federal building and deems references to it in existing records to use the new name. The tempting reading is that the word "regulation" signals rulemaking, but it merely lists a type of existing record and does not authorize or require any regulation. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.
fable.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States

qwen_block.w: This section simply designates the name of a federal building and updates references to it in federal records. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or requirements for outside input mentioned.

    (b) References.—Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the building referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the J. James Exon Federal Bureau of Investigation Building.

opus.w: This section only names a federal building and says that existing references to it, in any record, mean the new name. The word "regulation" is listed as one kind of record. It does not authorize or require rulemaking, so it does not count as participation. No one outside the federal government is consulted or given a role in any decision.
opus.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the building referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the J. James Exon Federal Bureau of Investigation Building.
opus.b:
**Step 1.** One tempting reading is that the word "regulation" in subsection (b) signals rulemaking. It doesn't. The section only says that existing references in records, including regulations, will mean the newly named building. It gives no agency authority to issue rules and sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body or consultation with anyone outside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply designates the name of a federal building. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or experts) in making this decision. The designation is made directly by statute.
qwen_chat.s: The Federal Bureau of Investigation building under construction at the intersection of 120th and L Streets in Omaha, Nebraska, shall be known and designated as the “J. James Exon Federal Bureau of Investigation Building”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that naming a building after a person involves some form of public recognition or consultation, but the text itself contains no procedural requirement for outside parties to participate in the decision to name the building. It is a unilateral legislative designation.
